# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 19 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_019_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 11

**1** He answered me: "Listen and understand. The stones from the plain placed in the building — those that were square, white, and fitting at the joints — represent the apostles, bishops, teachers, and deacons who walked in the holiness of God and served in their various offices with purity and reverence for God's chosen. Some have already fallen asleep; others still live. They were always in agreement with one another, lived at peace, and listened to each other. That is why their joints fit so precisely in the tower." **2** "Those dragged from the deep sea and placed in the building — these are those who suffered for the name of the Lord." **3** "And those brought from the mountains?" "These are believers who are not new to the faith — those found faithful throughout their entire lives, honored among God's people. **4** But those from the first mountain, which was black — these are apostates and traitors of the church, blasphemers against the Lord in their sinning, and those ashamed of the name of the Lord. These are dead to God; they cannot be placed in the building. They are of no use." **5** "Those from the second mountain, which was bare — these are hypocrites and teachers of evil who corrupt God's servants, especially those who are weak in sin; they have no room for repentance to move upward, but blasphemous words remain in their mouths. These may perhaps be stones, but barely."

---

*LOGOS note: Mountains 1 and 2 represent the most severe spiritual failures — apostasy/betrayal and active corruption of others. The final line "stones of the building, but only barely" suggests the barest possible inclusion or perhaps outright exclusion.*
